text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- New, voluntary system is being decided in which private sector companies and sellers of cotton can sell, gin or export their yields. The producer has the right to sell his yield to whomever he wants if export prices rise, and the state will bear the difference when the price falls from the guaranteed level.
- Export Import Bank of Japan report says that Egypt has reached an advanced stage in encouraging investment.

- Egyptian Ambassador to Israel Mohammed Bassiouni stresses that the peace process must not stop despite the existence of difficulties and illegal measures not conducive to the process. Confidence-building measures are underway for Palestinians and Israelis.

- After an 11-year ban, slaughtered chickens and birds are now allowed to be imported, says a decree from Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily. Chicken producers are seeking measures to ensure there is no glut in the market and to protect local investment.
- Higher Council for Exports will meet in the coming days to discuss encouraging small exporters, tariff exemptions, bank facilities and sales taxes.
- There is concern in United States markets over Egypt's decision to prohibit import of commodities which have been subject to genetic engineering.
